description: apcore Module -> OpenAI function definition, as built by OpenAIConverter.convert_descriptor(). This is where dot-to-hyphen normalization, x-llm-description promotion and x- extension stripping live: OpenAI function names must match ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$, so the module id is normalized, and the strict conversion rewrites the schema. The MCP path does none of this (see tool_mapping.json).
assertion_note: Field-level assertions rather than a whole-object comparison: the three bridges are known to differ in how they join annotation sections into the description, and pinning that byte-for-byte would assert a formatting accident rather than the mapping rule.

test_cases.description: Dots become hyphens because OpenAI function names may not contain dots. This is the normalization SRS 1560 reserves hyphens for.
Under strict conversion, x-llm-description replaces description so the model reads the AI-specific text.

token.x-llm-description: Long AI-specific description of the token

expected_property_description.value: Long AI-specific description of the token

test_cases.description: Under strict conversion, x- vendor extensions are removed so no internal metadata reaches the model.
F-041: mcp_-prefixed keys from annotations.extra are surfaced with the prefix stripped; other extra keys are not. Substring assertions, because the three bridges join the sections differently.

known_gaps.description: Python and TypeScript drive this fixture; Rust does not yet. The Rust OpenAIConverter exposes only convert_registry* — there is no convert_descriptor — so a driver must build a Registry and register a module before it can convert one descriptor. Worth doing, but it is a different shape of test than the other two bridges need.
